reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The request asks that the stem rules let a criterion cover "the standard Steward bullet". The reading's criterion 4 defines the standard bullets as 'a test that fails before the change and passes after it; fmt, clippy and test pass; no unrelated behavior changes'. The bullets Steward actually generates (steward.rs:620-624), and the ones in this request's own Acceptance list, are 'The change is made as described: <title>', 'No unrelated behavior changes; the existing tests pass' and 'fmt, clippy and test pass'. The long-title 'as described' bullet is the hard case for stem matching, and the reading leaves it out. (round 1 of 5). I read checks.rs (refusing_check and its step! macro), topics.rs (is_bullet, request_text_acceptance), steward.rs (from_change), replay.rs and the parser cases in refusal_corpus.rs. The plan's structure holds up. It adds a new step at the end of refusing_check, adds a separate request_parts parser so plan, steward and hestia acceptance stay unchanged, rewrites the two not-read-today cases, and leaves the reader rules unchanged within the budget. The named files, functions and line anchors exist. Two soundness problems need a revision. First, the plan's demonstration for criterion 4 uses bullet text I could not find in steward.rs, so it does not test the real standard Steward bullet. That bullet is "The change is made as described: <title>" (steward.rs:621). Under the ceil(n/2) threshold, a typical title would need about 9 of its stems to appear in a single criterion. By my hand count, this job's own request and accepted reading would then be refused. The replay at verification would probably also hold the change above its declared 5%. Second, the split exemption fires on bare common words such as `split` and `separately` anywhere in the request, so many ordinary refactoring requests would turn the check off. Smaller points: the 5% estimate has no stated basis, cited text that Athena's generators copy into requests can hold numbered lines, and "distinctive stem" is not defined. Findings: minor: crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-agent/src/fake.rs); major: The coverage threshold refuses the real standard Steward bullet, and the criterion-4 demo uses invented bullet text, so the test does not cover critic finding 2 (Decision 3 / Demonstration for criterion 4; crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs:620-624); major: The request-wide split exemption fires on common words, so many requests switch the check off by accident (Decision 6 / Step 2 (request_allows_split)); minor: The 5% estimate has no stated basis, and the replay holds the change if the real share is higher (Criterion 7 / checks.rs doc comment, 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'); minor: Text that Athena's generators copy into requests can hold numbered lines that are not parts (Decision 5 / Step 1 (numbered runs count anywhere outside quotes)); minor: 'Distinctive stem' is not defined (Step 1 ('each entry holds a distinctive stem'))
